why: Klarna could re-hire the 700 people it fired. MarketSquare starts at zero humans, so it has no bench to fall back to. The seam where a human will one day stand must therefore be DESIGNED and TESTED while it is still empty. Every AI decision surface below declares: what a wrong answer costs, the machine fallback that exists today, the human role that takes over when the machine is not enough, and the MEASURABLE trigger that says the seam must now be filled.

classes.RED: Irreversible harm to a person or to the trust promise. A wrong answer cannot be undone by a refund.
classes.AMBER: Money, ranking or reputation. Recoverable, but it costs real trust to recover.
classes.GREEN: Cosmetic or retryable. A wrong answer is an annoyance, the user retries.

surfaces.decides: Whether an ID document matches the claimed name
surfaces.cost_of_wrong: False accept lets a fraudster wear a verified badge; false reject locks an honest seller out with no appeal path
surfaces.machine_fallback: AI seam + circuit breaker; lane swap on outage
surfaces.trigger: ANY false accept discovered, OR >2% appeal rate on rejects, OR >40 verifications/week

surfaces.decides: Which copy and which photo regions carry identity and must be removed
surfaces.cost_of_wrong: A leaked phone number destroys the anonymity guarantee AND bypasses the intro fee -- the business model itself
surfaces.machine_fallback: Confidence gate; below-threshold held for manual review; nothing auto-publishes; first N imports spot-checked
surfaces.human_role: Import spot-checker (already assumed in the spec -- currently David)
surfaces.trigger: Second agency onboarded, OR >20 imports/week, OR any leak found in production

surfaces.cost_of_wrong: Degrading or unlawful imagery reaching buyers; or an honest seller silently censored
surfaces.machine_fallback: Refuse rather than blur-to-ruin (RG-0040/0044/0047); judged by bytes not declared type
surfaces.trigger: First refusal appeal, OR any reported image that passed, OR >100 uploads/day

surfaces.decides: When a user's Tuppence is spent
surfaces.cost_of_wrong: Charging for a service not delivered -- the fastest possible way to lose a founding seller
surfaces.machine_fallback: Charge on delivery only (RG-0033); spend reserved before dispatch (RG-0037); daily ceilings
surfaces.human_role: Billing dispute handler (David until volume forces otherwise)

surfaces.decides: Graded condition (Near Mint..Damaged) which drives price
surfaces.cost_of_wrong: Buyer receives a card worse than graded -- collectables communities punish this publicly and permanently
surfaces.machine_fallback: None declared -- the grade is emitted as fact
surfaces.human_role: Collectables moderator (a founding seller, paid in Tuppence)
surfaces.trigger: BUILD NOW: any grade above a value threshold must carry 'AI-assisted estimate, not a certified grade' and a dispute route

surfaces.decides: Whether a listed price is fair
surfaces.cost_of_wrong: A confident wrong price anchors a seller low (lost money) or high (dead listing)
surfaces.trigger: BUILD NOW: label as opinion with a range, never a number presented as fact

surfaces.cost_of_wrong: Reads as financial advice; regulatory and reputational exposure well beyond the listing
surfaces.human_role: Escalate to partnered agent -- this is precisely the introduction MarketSquare sells
surfaces.trigger: BUILD NOW: disclaimer + agency hand-off on every yield output

surfaces.cost_of_wrong: A legal notice classified as spam. This is the Klarna failure exactly: volume handled, complexity missed
surfaces.machine_fallback: Classification only; escalation_brief.py renders LEGAL/MONEY/COST/TRUST for David
surfaces.trigger: HARD RULE: nothing classified legal/billing ever auto-sends. Human seam at >30 inbound/day

surfaces.decides: The title and description a buyer reads
surfaces.cost_of_wrong: Misdescription is a consumer-law problem, not a copy problem, once money moves
surfaces.machine_fallback: Seller reviews and publishes -- the human seam is the SELLER and it already exists
surfaces.human_role: Seller (already in the loop) + copy reviewer at scale
surfaces.trigger: Only if drafts ever auto-publish. They must not.

surfaces.decides: How a seller should raise their trust score
surfaces.cost_of_wrong: Teaches sellers to farm the rubric -- see the incentive register, IL-02
surfaces.machine_fallback: Published rubric; no signal self-reported without verification
surfaces.trigger: Any signal earnable without evidence going live

surfaces.decides: Classifies faults, proposes and (when armed) ships code patches
surfaces.cost_of_wrong: An autonomous agent shipping to the live site is the single highest-blast-radius surface in the system
surfaces.machine_fallback: Default OFF; shadow mode; MAX_SHIPS_PER_HOUR; ledger+predeploy+BIT gates; server auto-rollback; REFUSE_LEGAL_COSTLY / REFUSE_TRUST_CORE force escalation
surfaces.human_role: David (TOTAL AUTONOMY ruling 29 Jul 2026 retired the per-change veto in favour of mechanical gates)
surfaces.trigger: REVIEW: the no-veto ruling is correct only while the mechanical gates are provably complete. Any gate that stops asserting re-arms the veto.

surfaces.decides: Turns free text into a query -- shapes what a buyer sees
surfaces.cost_of_wrong: Buyer sees the wrong things and retries; invisible failure if it silently hides a category

surfaces.decides: Which listings match a wishlist and get pushed
surfaces.cost_of_wrong: Bad matches train buyers to ignore notifications permanently
surfaces.machine_fallback: Deterministic keyword matcher today; AI socket is hot-swappable
surfaces.trigger: Before swapping the deterministic matcher for AI, run BOTH in parallel and compare -- do not switch off the old one

surfaces.decides: Coaching and market commentary shown to the seller
surfaces.machine_fallback: Charged 1T after first free use, so a bad one costs the seller money
surfaces.trigger: Refund rate on coach charges above 5%

incentive_register.test: THE DRAGON TAIL TEST. Dragon Tail never malfunctioned. It gave independent economic agents perfect information and was surprised when they used it perfectly. For every surface where a third party can see platform-internal information, ask: if this actor optimises purely for themselves, what emerges? Then check the emergent behaviour is one MarketSquare can survive.

leaks.if_they_optimise: Enumerate emails, profile who is spending, target high-balance sellers
leaks.today: Masked only by the pre-launch edge gate, which LIFTS AT LAUNCH
leaks.action: Authenticate before launch. This is a launch blocker, not a nice-to-have.

leaks.surface: Trust score rubric fully published, tiers and thresholds public (Gold 90+ = featured priority)
leaks.if_they_optimise: Farm the cheapest points to hit 90 without becoming more trustworthy; referral lane is the obvious vector (specced, evidence_required varies)
leaks.today: Defence is 'no signal self-reported without verification, none client-modifiable'
leaks.action: Before referrals go live, they need evidence. Publishing the rubric is right -- publishing an unverified signal is not.

leaks.surface: Boost lowers the match threshold 60 -> 45 and sorts boosted-first
leaks.if_they_optimise: Boost weak listings to reach buyers they should not reach; buyers learn boosted results are worse and stop trusting the feed
leaks.today: Thresholds live in code but are inferable from behaviour
leaks.action: Boost should raise VISIBILITY, never lower RELEVANCE. Decouple the two. Add a ledger entry.

leaks.surface: Intro costs the seller 1T, 2T if boosted -- pay-to-be-reachable
leaks.if_they_optimise: Sellers suppress boost to pay less and become less reachable; buyers with Trust <20 or in cooldown route around the platform
leaks.today: LM-T1 first-intro idempotency, LM-15 trust gate, LM-F3 7-day cooldown
leaks.action: Watch for the emergent case: any incentive that makes a seller LESS reachable works against the only thing the till charges for.

leaks.surface: Anonymisation is the only thing standing between an agency and a free bypass of the intro fee
leaks.if_they_optimise: Probe the anonymiser for the copy pattern that survives it
leaks.action: Treat anonymiser bypass as an adversarial-testing target, not a QA case. The agency is an independent economic agent, exactly like a DoorDash driver.

leaks.surface: super_example exemplars pinned first in every sort
leaks.if_they_optimise: Conclude the platform favours its own demos and disengage
leaks.today: RG-0052 asserts the banner shows and the pin is not stolen from real sellers
leaks.action: Holding. Re-check the moment real listing volume passes demo volume.

predesign_rules.detail: No AI surface replaces a working mechanism without both running side by side and their outputs compared under real load. Applies most directly to HS-13 (deterministic matcher -> AI). This is the single rule that would have saved both companies in the video.
Every RED and AMBER surface declares its human role and its measurable trigger BEFORE a human exists. Klarna had a bench to rehire; MarketSquare has none, so the seam must be pre-cut.

predesign_rules.rule: NEVER REMOVE THE FALLBACK AND ADD THE AI IN THE SAME CHANGE
predesign_rules.detail: Yum mandated Dragon Tail AND centralised the DoorDash contract simultaneously, so the franchise lost the AI's replacement and its own manual tools at once. One change at a time; the old lane stays until the new one has proven itself in production.

predesign_rules.rule: RUN THE DRAGON TAIL TEST ON EVERY NEW INFORMATION SURFACE
predesign_rules.detail: Before exposing any platform-internal signal to sellers, buyers, agencies or affiliates, write down what a purely self-interested actor does with it. If the answer is unknown, it is not ready to ship.

predesign_rules.rule: NO PUBLIC CLAIM THE MACHINERY CANNOT YET HONOUR
predesign_rules.detail: Klarna's real loss was narrative: it went to the public market on an AI-first thesis and reversed within ten weeks. MarketSquare's copy must never promise a capability that is currently a hope. Vendor-neutral AI copy (RG-0035) is the same discipline -- extend it to capability claims.

predesign_rules.rule: HIRING HUMANS IS A PLANNED MILESTONE, NOT A RETREAT
predesign_rules.detail: Because MarketSquare is AI-first BY DESIGN rather than by cost-cutting, adding humans at a declared trigger is the design working, not the design failing. Say so in advance, publicly and internally, so the first hire never reads as a Klarna-style U-turn.
